Quotas & billing {{ds:component/chip|label=v2|variant=primary}} {{ds:component/chip|label=Stable|variant=success}}

Godzilla accounts operate under usage quotas determined by your plan tier. Quotas apply at the workspace level across API request throughput, monthly event volume, and concurrent pipeline resources.

Plan tiers

Each workspace is assigned to a tier that dictates default rate limits and monthly event capacities.

Plan Rate limit Monthly events Active pipelines Support SLA
Starter 100 req / min 50,000 3 Community
Standard 1,000 req / min 1,000,000 25 1 business day
Enterprise Custom (10,000+ req / min) Custom / Unlimited Unlimited 24/7 dedicated SLA

What happens when you exceed a quota

Exceeding limits is handled differently depending on whether you exceed a per-minute API request rate or a monthly event volume quota.

API rate limits (HTTP 429)

If your application sends more requests in a one-minute window than your tier allows, the API returns a 429 Too Many Requests status code. Responses include a Retry-After header indicating how many seconds to wait before resuming requests. See Rate limits for header details and retry strategies.

Monthly event quotas

Monthly event usage resets on the first day of your billing cycle. When approaching or exceeding event limits:

  • 80% and 100% threshold alerts: Account admins receive email notifications and webhook lifecycle events (workspace.quota_warning) when approaching your limit.
  • Standard plan overages: On the Standard tier, pipelines continue running without interruption. Overage events are billed at $0.15 per 10,000 events on your next invoice.
  • Starter plan cap: Starter tier workspaces pause pipeline ingestion once the 50,000 event limit is reached until the next billing cycle or an upgrade to Standard.

Resource limits (pipelines and connectors)

If you attempt to create more active pipelines or connectors than your plan allows, the API returns a 403 Forbidden with code quota_exceeded.

Upgrading and quota increases

You can upgrade your plan or add billing details directly from workspace settings. If your workload requires higher burst rate limits or tailored enterprise terms, reach out via Troubleshooting / FAQ.

{{ds:component/card|href={{cms:item/0881cc13-706b-45dc-b215-08b706dc8fdb}}|tag=Concept|title=Pipelines|description=Named, versioned workflows that move data from a source to a destination through optional transforms.}} {{ds:component/card|href={{cms:item/c5b993ae-0d23-4b29-9765-4fef876734ee}}|tag=Concept|title=Connectors|description=Pre-built integrations to external systems — sources, destinations, or both.}} {{ds:component/card|href={{cms:item/aaba4e33-be69-4693-8066-1c2f622b674b}}|tag=Concept|title=Events|description=The atomic unit of data flowing through a pipeline, plus the platform's own lifecycle events.}} {{ds:component/card|href={{cms:item/88ecedb3-543b-4dcf-b985-6fb94e4eaa95}}|tag=Concept|title=Schemas|description=Declarative contracts that define and validate the structure of event payloads flowing through pipelines.}}

How they fit together

A pipeline reads events from a source connector, validates their schemas, transforms them, and writes them to a destination connector. Everything else in Godzilla — retries, webhooks, monitoring — is built on top of that single loop.

Definitions

Short definitions for every term used throughout these docs.

Pipeline
A named, versioned workflow that moves data from a source connector, through optional transforms, to a destination connector. See the Pipelines endpoint for API operations.
Connector
A pre-built integration to an external system — a source, a destination, or both. Manage credentials and health in the Connectors endpoint.
Event
The atomic unit of data moving through a pipeline, or a platform lifecycle notification like pipeline.failed. Query and replay them via the Events endpoint.
Schema
A declarative contract specifying the structure, types, and validation rules for event payloads.
Webhook
An outbound HTTP request Godzilla sends to a URL you control when a subscribed event occurs.
Dead-letter queue
Where an event goes after exhausting its retries, rather than being dropped. See Error handling & recovery.

Pipelines

A pipeline is the core unit of work in Godzilla: a named, versioned data-processing workflow that moves data from a source connector, through zero or more transform steps, to a destination connector. Every pipeline runs as a sequence of events flowing through that path.

Anatomy of a pipeline

Every pipeline has three parts:

  • Source — the connector that emits events into the pipeline (a database, a queue, an upload, a webhook).
  • Transforms — an ordered list of steps that reshape, filter, or enrich events as they pass through. Transforms are optional; a pipeline with none is a pass-through copy.
  • Destination — the connector that events are written to once transforms complete.
{{ds:component/alert|variant=info|title=Pipelines are declarative|body_html=

You describe the desired source, transforms, and destination; Godzilla schedules and retries the runs. You never manage worker processes directly.

}}

Pipeline state

A pipeline is always in one of three states:

  • draft — configured but not yet processing events.
  • active — running on its configured schedule or trigger.
  • paused — temporarily stopped; resumes from the last checkpoint.

Versioning

Pipeline configuration is versioned. Publishing a new version does not affect events already in flight on the previous version — in-flight runs finish on the version they started on. This matters most when a pipeline definition is part of a larger migration; see the Migration guide for an example of retiring an old pipeline version safely.

Next steps

Ready to build one? Start with the Building your first pipeline guide, or jump straight to the Pipelines endpoint in the API reference.

Events

An event is the atomic unit of data that moves through a pipeline. Every record a source connector emits, every row a transform produces, and every write a destination connector performs is an event.

Event shape

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=event.json|language=json|code={ "id": "evt_8f2c1a90", "type": "order.created", "occurred_at": "2026-08-18T09:12:44Z", "source": "connector_postgres_orders", "payload": { "order_id": "ord_4471", "amount_cents": 4899 } }}}

Payload schemas & validation

The payload property contains the user data carried by the event. You can declare contract definitions for event payload shapes using Schemas. Godzilla validates payloads at ingress, transform, and egress boundaries to ensure data matches expected types and required attributes.

User data events vs. platform events

Godzilla distinguishes two kinds of events:

  • User data events — the records your pipelines process, shaped however your source system produces them.
  • Platform events — lifecycle notifications Godzilla itself emits: pipeline.started, pipeline.completed, pipeline.failed, connector.error. These are what power Webhooks.
{{ds:component/alert|variant=info|title=Ordering|body_html=

Events are delivered in-order per source partition, not globally. Two events from different source partitions may be processed out of order relative to each other.

}}

Retries and dead-lettering

An event that fails a transform or destination write is retried with exponential backoff. After the configured retry limit, it is moved to that pipeline's dead-letter queue rather than dropped. See Error handling & recovery for how to configure and drain a dead-letter queue.

See also

To query or replay events programmatically via the REST API, see the Events endpoint in the API reference.

A connector is a pre-built integration to an external system that a Pipeline reads from or writes to. Connectors handle authentication, batching, and retry behavior for a specific system so pipeline authors don't have to.

  • Bidirectional — a small set of connectors, like the generic Webhook connector, can act as either.

Schemas

A schema is a declarative contract that defines the expected structure, data types, and required fields for an event payload moving through a pipeline. Schemas prevent malformed records from propagating downstream and ensure data integrity across source and destination connectors.

Declaring a schema

Godzilla schemas follow standard JSON Schema (Draft-07) specifications. You define schemas per event type or attach them directly to pipeline ingress and egress stages.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=order-created.schema.json|language=json|code={ "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", "title": "OrderCreatedPayload", "type": "object", "properties": { "order_id": { "type": "string" }, "customer_id": { "type": "string" }, "amount_cents": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 0 }, "currency": { "type": "string", "enum": ["USD", "EUR", "GBP"] }, "status": { "type": "string" } }, "required": ["order_id", "amount_cents", "currency"], "additionalProperties": false }}}

Validation & enforcement modes

When a pipeline processes an event, Godzilla validates the payload against the registered schema. You can configure how validation failures are handled using one of three enforcement modes:

  • strict — Any event failing validation is immediately rejected and routed to the pipeline's dead-letter queue.
  • warn — The event continues through the pipeline, but a platform warning event is emitted for monitoring and alerting.
  • drop — Invalid events are silently discarded without halting pipeline execution or triggering retries.
{{ds:component/alert|variant=warning|title=Validation failure handling|body_html=

In strict mode, validation errors do not retry endlessly. Because payload schema mismatches are deterministic, failed events bypass transient retries and move straight to the dead-letter queue. See Error handling & recovery for details on inspecting and replaying dead-lettered events.

}}

Schema validation in the pipeline lifecycle

Validation can occur at three points in a pipeline run:

  1. Ingress validation — Verified immediately after a source connector emits an event, ensuring source data conforms to expectations.
  2. Post-transform validation — Verified after transform steps run to confirm reshaped payloads match target specifications.
  3. Egress validation — Checked before writing to a destination connector to guarantee downstream compatibility.

Schema evolution & compatibility

As business requirements change, schemas evolve. Godzilla supports backward and forward compatibility rules to prevent breaking active pipelines:

  • Additive changes — Adding optional fields is backward-compatible and does not require pipeline downtime.
  • Breaking changes — Removing fields or adding new required fields requires creating a new pipeline version or using a transform step to migrate payload shapes.

Troubleshooting / FAQ

Common problems, and where in the docs to go for the full explanation.

My pipeline isn't processing events

Check the source connector's health field via the Connectors endpoint. A down connector stalls every pipeline that reads from it. If it's healthy, confirm the pipeline itself is active and not paused — see Scheduling & triggers.

Events keep failing and landing in the dead-letter queue

Walk through Error handling & recovery — it covers both diagnosing the failure and replaying events once fixed.

I'm not receiving webhook deliveries

Verify your endpoint returns a 2xx status and that you're checking X-Godzilla-Signature correctly — a rejected signature looks identical to a dropped delivery from the outside. Full details in the Webhooks endpoint reference.

I'm getting 429s

You've hit the standard-tier limit described in Rate limits. Back off using the Retry-After header, or review Quotas & billing to learn about plan tiers and how overages are handled.

{{ds:component/alert|variant=warning|title=Migrating from v1?|body_html=

A number of "it worked yesterday" reports trace back to v1's offset pagination or polling patterns carried over into v2 code. See the Migration guide.

Scheduling & triggers

A pipeline runs either on a schedule or in response to incoming events. This guide covers both.

Scheduled pipelines

Set a schedule (a cron expression) when creating or updating a pipeline via the Pipelines endpoint. Godzilla runs the pipeline once per schedule tick, processing whatever new data is available from the source since the last run.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=schedule.json|language=json|code={ \"schedule\": \"0 */4 * * *\" }}}

Event-triggered pipelines

Omit schedule and the pipeline instead runs continuously, processing events as its source connector emits them — the right choice for sources like Kafka or a Webhook connector where near-real-time matters.

{{ds:component/alert|variant=info|title=Choosing between them|body_html=

Use a schedule for sources that batch naturally (a nightly file drop to S3). Use event-triggered for anything where minutes matter.

}}

Pausing and resuming

A paused pipeline skips scheduled ticks entirely and buffers nothing for event-triggered sources — resuming picks up new events going forward, not a backlog. To reprocess a time range instead, see the replay flow in Error handling & recovery.

{{ds:component/docs-pagination|prev_href={{cms:item/5d223f1f-d8d7-4a1c-84a2-0572aa6292ba}}|prev_label=Error handling & recovery|next_href={{cms:item/2cc70b4c-dee1-472a-8b09-9974e1ecd1fb}}|next_label=Monitoring & alerts}}", "version_token": "223fb45f-9e2c-436e-8560-88d0b077c55a", "created_at": "2026-08-22T01:09:42.089Z", "updated_at": "2026-08-22T01:09:54.591Z", "placement_id": "8ed279da-c9eb-46e0-bd2f-4f15df9f1c76", "folder_id": "c3e0ba4a-a491-4265-9848-556d298e6b6b", "file_name": "scheduling-and-triggers" } }

Error handling & recovery

Every event that fails a transform or a destination write is retried automatically. This guide covers how that works and what to do when retries run out.

Automatic retries

Failed events retry with exponential backoff — 1s, 2s, 4s, up to a per-pipeline configurable ceiling. Most transient failures (a destination hiccup, a rate-limited third party) resolve within the first few attempts.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=pipeline-retry-config.json|language=json|code={ \"retry_policy\": { \"max_attempts\": 5, \"backoff\": \"exponential\", \"initial_delay_ms\": 1000 } }}}

Dead-lettering

An event that exhausts its retries is moved to that pipeline's dead-letter queue rather than dropped silently.

{{ds:component/alert|variant=danger|title=Dead-lettered events don't retry themselves|body_html=

Once in the dead-letter queue, an event stays there until you replay it or explicitly discard it — it will not retry again on its own.

}}

Replaying events

Use the Events endpoint's replay action to re-run a specific dead-lettered event once the underlying issue is fixed.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=replay.sh|language=bash|code=curl -X POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v3/events/evt_8f2c1a90/replay \ -H \"Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY\"}}

Watching for failures

Subscribe to pipeline.failed via Webhooks so you find out about dead-lettered events before a customer does. See also Monitoring & alerts.

{ "item": { "id": "34f15418-1e32-455b-8b41-2f0bc73f5b68", "content_type": "generic", "workflow_state": "public", "page_title": "Backfill historical data", "short_description": "Techniques and configurations for loading historical data ranges through Godzilla pipelines.", "body": "

Backfill historical data

Backfilling lets you stream historical data from your storage or database into downstream targets — bootstrapping new destinations, backpopulating historical records, or replaying data after schema changes.

{{ds:component/alert|variant=info|title=Before you begin|body_html=

Ensure your source connector supports range queries or timestamp filtering. See Connecting a data source for connector details.

}}

1. Define a time-bounded source connector

Configure your source connector with start and end timestamps (or watermarks) to define the historical boundary. This prevents the backfill job from processing live events prematurely.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=backfill-source.json|language=json|code={ \"type\": \"postgres\", \"direction\": \"source\", \"config\": { \"connection_string\": \"postgres://user:secret@db.example.com:5432/production\", \"query\": \"SELECT * FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2025-01-01T00:00:00Z' AND created_at < '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z'\", \"timestamp_column\": \"created_at\" } }}}

2. Set batch size and concurrency controls

Historical backfills often involve large data volumes. Adjust your pipeline's batch size and concurrency limit to avoid exhausting memory or triggering rate limits on your destination system.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=pipeline-backfill.json|language=json|code={ \"name\": \"orders-backfill-2025\", \"source_connector_id\": \"conn_pg_orders_backfill\", \"destination_connector_id\": \"conn_snowflake_dw\", \"settings\": { \"batch_size\": 5000, \"concurrency\": 4, \"max_retries\": 5 } }}} {{ds:component/alert|variant=warning|title=Destination throughput|body_html=

Monitor destination write latency while the backfill runs. If destination response times spike, reduce pipeline concurrency.

}}

3. Run and monitor the backfill

Start the pipeline using the Pipelines endpoint. You can inspect event throughput and error rates via Monitoring & alerts.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=run-backfill.sh|language=bash|code=curl -X POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/pipelines/orders-backfill-2025/start \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY\"}}

4. Transitioning to real-time streaming

Once the backfill reaches the cutoff timestamp, switch the pipeline configuration or activate your real-time streaming pipeline. Godzilla ensures idempotent writes when keys are configured, preventing duplicate entries during handoff.

Next steps

Learn how to handle failed records during backfills in Error handling & recovery, or query processed records using the Events endpoint.

args.body:
Backfill historical data

Backfilling lets you stream historical data from your storage or database into downstream targets — bootstrapping new destinations, backpopulating historical records, or replaying data after schema changes.

{{ds:component/alert|variant=info|title=Before you begin|body_html=

Ensure your source connector supports range queries or timestamp filtering. See Connecting a data source for connector details.

}}

1. Define a time-bounded source connector

Configure your source connector with start and end timestamps (or watermarks) to define the historical boundary. This prevents the backfill job from processing live events prematurely.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=backfill-source.json|language=json|code={ "type": "postgres", "direction": "source", "config": { "connection_string": "postgres://user:secret@db.example.com:5432/production", "query": "SELECT * FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2025-01-01T00:00:00Z' AND created_at < '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z'", "timestamp_column": "created_at" } }}}

2. Set batch size and concurrency controls

Historical backfills often involve large data volumes. Adjust your pipeline's batch size and concurrency limit to avoid exhausting memory or triggering rate limits on your destination system.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=pipeline-backfill.json|language=json|code={ "name": "orders-backfill-2025", "source_connector_id": "conn_pg_orders_backfill", "destination_connector_id": "conn_snowflake_dw", "settings": { "batch_size": 5000, "concurrency": 4, "max_retries": 5 } }}} {{ds:component/alert|variant=warning|title=Destination throughput|body_html=

Monitor destination write latency while the backfill runs. If destination response times spike, reduce pipeline concurrency.

}}

3. Run and monitor the backfill

Start the pipeline using the Pipelines endpoint. You can inspect event throughput and error rates via Monitoring & alerts.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=run-backfill.sh|language=bash|code=curl -X POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v3/pipelines/orders-backfill-2025/start \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY"}}

4. Transitioning to real-time streaming

Once the backfill reaches the cutoff timestamp, switch the pipeline configuration or activate your real-time streaming pipeline. Godzilla ensures idempotent writes when keys are configured, preventing duplicate entries during handoff.

Next steps

Learn how to handle failed records during backfills in Error handling & recovery, or query processed records using the Events endpoint.

Migration guide (v1 → v2) {{ds:component/chip|label=v1 retired|variant=danger}}

v1 reached end of life on 2026-08-01 alongside the webhooks GA changelog entry. This guide covers the key breaking changes you need to handle to move a v1 integration over.

{{ds:component/alert|variant=warning|title=Pipelines and Events endpoints are on v3|body_html=

Both the Pipelines endpoint and Events endpoint now have a v3. Version 3 is the current version for pipelines (with v2 Pipelines deprecated), and the v2 events endpoint has been withdrawn entirely. When migrating, target the v3 endpoints (/v3/pipelines, /v3/pipelines/{pipeline_id}/events, and /v3/events/{id}/replay) directly.

}}

1. Pagination: offset → cursor

v1 used page/per_page query parameters. List endpoints in the current API use an opaque cursor and next_cursor — see Rate limits for the exact envelope.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=diff|language=diff|code=- GET /v1/pipelines?page=2&per_page=20 + GET /v3/pipelines?cursor=eyJvZmZzZXQiOjIwfQ}}

2. Status checks: polling → webhooks

v1 had no push notifications — you polled a pipeline's status endpoint. Godzilla replaces this with the Webhooks endpoint: subscribe to pipeline.completed and pipeline.failed instead of polling.

3. Error shape

v1 returned bare error strings. Godzilla wraps every error in an object with a stable code field. Update any error handling that matched on message text — see the error shape reference.

{{ds:component/alert|variant=danger|title=v1 is retired|body_html=

v1 endpoints no longer accept requests. If you're seeing 404s on /v1/* paths, that's why — there is no grace-period fallback.

}}

Still stuck?

Common migration issues are covered in Troubleshooting / FAQ.

args.body:
{{ds:component/hero|title=Concepts|subtitle=The core building blocks every Godzilla pipeline is made of.|cta_html=Start with Pipelines}}

Godzilla is built from core concepts that compose into everything else in these docs. Understanding how they relate makes the rest of the platform — guides, API reference, SDKs — much easier to follow.

{{ds:component/card|href={{cms:item/4140d058-72b1-4c9d-8e6e-5c87f2f8622f}}|tag=Concept|title=Pipelines|description=Named, versioned workflows that move data from a source to a destination through optional transforms.}} {{ds:component/card|href={{cms:item/8f0aa371-ceaa-4f95-9501-ed9045d5921a}}|tag=Concept|title=Connectors|description=Pre-built integrations to external systems — sources, destinations, or both.}} {{ds:component/card|href={{cms:item/6ab8d898-f580-4482-8103-20651f83e320}}|tag=Concept|title=Events|description=The atomic unit of data flowing through a pipeline, plus the platform's own lifecycle events.}} {{ds:component/card|href={{cms:item/0b64afcb-f953-48ce-b384-e8c013b343e3}}|tag=Concept|title=Schemas|description=Declarative contracts that define and validate the structure of event payloads flowing through pipelines.}}

How they fit together

A pipeline reads events from a source connector, validates their schemas, transforms them, and writes them to a destination connector. Everything else in Godzilla — retries, webhooks, monitoring — is built on top of that single loop.

Definitions

Short definitions for every term used throughout these docs.

Pipeline
A named, versioned workflow that moves data from a source connector, through optional transforms, to a destination connector. See the Pipelines endpoint for API operations.
Connector
A pre-built integration to an external system — a source, a destination, or both. Manage credentials and health in the Connectors endpoint.
Event
The atomic unit of data moving through a pipeline, or a platform lifecycle notification like pipeline.failed. Query and replay them via the Events endpoint.
Schema
A declarative contract specifying the structure, types, and validation rules for event payloads.
Webhook
An outbound HTTP request Godzilla sends to a URL you control when a subscribed event occurs.
Dead-letter queue
Where an event goes after exhausting its retries, rather than being dropped. See Error handling & recovery.
Cursor pagination
The pagination style used by every list endpoint across the API (including v2 and v3). See Rate limits.
Quota
Usage allowances assigned to a workspace based on its plan tier, covering request throughput and monthly event volume. See Quotas & billing.
Workspace
The top-level account boundary an API key is scoped to.

Rate limits {{ds:component/chip|label=v2 / v3|variant=primary}} {{ds:component/chip|label=Stable|variant=success}}

{{ds:component/stat|value=100|label=requests / minute (Starter)|description=Rate limit for Starter-tier API keys, per workspace.}} {{ds:component/stat|value=1,000|label=requests / minute (Standard)|description=Default rate limit for Standard-tier API keys, per workspace.}} {{ds:component/stat|value=10,000+|label=requests / minute (Enterprise)|description=Custom rate limit for Enterprise-tier API keys, per workspace.}}

Rate limit headers

Every response includes X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, and X-RateLimit-Reset. A request over the limit returns 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header.

To view limits across all plan tiers or what happens when an account exceeds its quota, see the Quotas & billing reference.

Pagination

List endpoints (Pipelines, Connectors, Events) use cursor-based pagination — a departure from v1's offset-based pagination.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=list-response.json|language=json|code={ \"data\": [ { \"id\": \"pl_ingest_orders\" } ], \"next_cursor\": \"eyJvZmZzZXQiOjIwfQ\", \"has_more\": true }}} {{ds:component/docs-toc|items_html=
  • Rate limit headers
  • Pagination

input.body:
{{ds:component/hero|title=Concepts|subtitle=The core building blocks every Godzilla pipeline is made of.|cta_html=Start with Pipelines}}

Godzilla is built from core concepts that compose into everything else in these docs. Understanding how they relate makes the rest of the platform — guides, API reference, SDKs — much easier to follow.

{{ds:component/card|href={{cms:item/4140d058-72b1-4c9d-8e6e-5c87f2f8622f}}|tag=Concept|title=Pipelines|description=Named, versioned workflows that move data from a source to a destination through optional transforms.}} {{ds:component/card|href={{cms:item/8f0aa371-ceaa-4f95-9501-ed9045d5921a}}|tag=Concept|title=Connectors|description=Pre-built integrations to external systems — sources, destinations, or both.}} {{ds:component/card|href={{cms:item/6ab8d898-f580-4482-8103-20651f83e320}}|tag=Concept|title=Events|description=The atomic unit of data flowing through a pipeline, plus the platform's own lifecycle events.}} {{ds:component/card|href={{cms:item/0b64afcb-f953-48ce-b384-e8c013b343e3}}|tag=Concept|title=Schemas|description=Declarative contracts that define and validate the structure of event payloads flowing through pipelines.}}

How they fit together

A pipeline reads events from a source connector, validates their schemas, transforms them, and writes them to a destination connector. Everything else in Godzilla — retries, webhooks, monitoring — is built on top of that single loop.

Definitions

Short definitions for every term used throughout these docs.

Pipeline
A named, versioned workflow that moves data from a source connector, through optional transforms, to a destination connector. See the Pipelines endpoint for API operations.
Connector
A pre-built integration to an external system — a source, a destination, or both. Manage credentials and health in the Connectors endpoint.
Event
The atomic unit of data moving through a pipeline, or a platform lifecycle notification like pipeline.failed. Query and replay them via the Events endpoint.
Schema
A declarative contract specifying the structure, types, and validation rules for event payloads.
Webhook
An outbound HTTP request Godzilla sends to a URL you control when a subscribed event occurs.
Dead-letter queue
Where an event goes after exhausting its retries, rather than being dropped. See Error handling & recovery.
Cursor pagination
The pagination style used by every list endpoint across the API (including v2 and v3). See Rate limits.
Quota
Usage allowances assigned to a workspace based on its plan tier, covering request throughput and monthly event volume. See Quotas & billing.
Workspace
The top-level account boundary an API key is scoped to.

2. **Getting Started Guides**:
   - **Installation** (`getting-started/getting-started-installation`): Updated direct cURL example to target `/v3/pipelines`.
   - **Quickstart** (`getting-started/getting-started-quickstart`): Updated pipeline creation example to target `POST /v3/pipelines`.
   - **Authentication** (`getting-started/getting-started-authentication`): Updated example endpoint call to `https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v3/pipelines`.
3. **Recipes**:
   - **Backfill historical data** (`recipes/backfill-historical-data`): Updated the pipeline execution cURL snippet to `POST /v3/pipelines/...`.
4. **Concepts & Reference**:
   - **Concepts** (`concepts`): Updated the cursor pagination definition to clarify applicability across v2 and v3 list endpoints.
   - **Rate limits** (`api/rate-limits-errors`): Updated chip and metadata to reflect coverage of the current Godzilla REST API across v2 and v3 endpoints.
   - **Error reference** (`api/error-reference`): Updated copy and chips to cover the consistent error shape across REST API versions.
5. **SDKs** (`sdks/index`, `sdks/go`, `sdks/node-js`, `sdks/python`):
